QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_125

question.text: What is the regulatory implication of physical settlement for stock futures positions held till expiry?

answer.text: Traders with open short futures positions must ensure they have the required shares in their demat account for delivery, or face non-fulfilment penalties, close-out, or other clearing-corporation action for short delivery
The clearing corporation converts the futures position into a spot market trade at a 5% discount to the settlement price
Physical settlement is optional; traders can always choose cash settlement by paying a 2% premium
Only FIIs and mutual funds are required to physically settle; retail traders can choose cash settlement

explanation.text: The Logic: Under physical settlement, a trader with an open short stock futures position at expiry must deliver the underlying shares, and so must have the required shares in the demat account. If the deliverable obligation is not fulfilled, the clearing corporation can take action including close-out, non-fulfilment penalties, and other steps for short delivery. Long futures holders must accept delivery and pay the settlement amount. This applies to all market participants (retail, institutional, FPIs). The Trap: There is no 5% discount conversion. Physical settlement is not optional, and all participants must physically settle, not just FIIs or mutual funds. The key risk is for short sellers who must arrange shares for delivery. Note: The exact phrase "auction penalty" was not located in the pages checked; the source supports clearing-corporation action and penalties for non-fulfilment of securities deliverable obligations.
